question: Sophie had $184 saved for a new laptop, while her friend Marcus had $95 saved for a tablet. Sophie earned $55 more from tutoring. She then earned $44 more from a part-time job. Her savings doubled when her grandparents matched her total as a graduation gift. She then earned $39 more from selling old textbooks. Finally, a scholarship program turned every dollar she had into 6 dollars. How much money did Sophie have after the scholarship program?

A donut shop had 98 donuts left after the morning rush. A delivery mishap caused 68 donuts to be sent to the wrong store. A batch fresh out of the fryer added a dozen more donuts to the case. A second batch added 32 more donuts. A third batch added 44 more donuts, all baked within '60 minutes, or one hour' of the lunch rush starting. A final afternoon batch added 19 more donuts. How many donuts were in the case after the final afternoon batch?

Marco had 222 vinyl records in his collection, while his sister Elena had 150 records in hers. Marco found 63 more records at a garage sale. A collector's trade then turned every record he had into 3 records. He then received 16 more records as a birthday gift. A rare estate sale turned every record into 3 more records, a deal that took '120 minutes, or two hours' to negotiate. Finally, he sold 490 records to a vintage shop. How many records did Marco have after selling to the vintage shop?

Amelia had 170 beads in her jewelry box, while her friend Zara had 90 beads in hers. Amelia used 55 beads to make a bracelet for her mom. She then bought 21 more beads at the craft store. A friend gave her 18 more beads for her birthday. Finally, she used 148 beads to make a large necklace for a craft fair. How many beads did Amelia have left after making the necklace?

A woodworking class had 64 blocks of wood at the start of the semester. The teacher mentioned that a dozen new saw blades had also arrived, though that had nothing to do with the wood block count. Students used 24 blocks for a group project, and a supply order then turned every remaining block into 9 blocks. The class donated 136 blocks to a community art project, and a second donation gave away 214 more blocks. Finally, a local lumberyard donated 43 more blocks. How many blocks of wood were left after the lumberyard's donation?

In the morning, a bakery had 102 muffins ready for sale. By midday, a catering order added 65 more muffins. In the afternoon, a wholesale account turned every muffin into 9 muffins to fill a big order, a batch that took '180 minutes, or three hours' to bake. The head baker mentioned a dozen new aprons had arrived for the staff, though that had nothing to do with the muffins. That evening, 3 more muffins were baked as samples. Right before closing, 7 more muffins were added from a final tray. How many muffins were there after the final tray was added?

In the morning, a farm stand had 116 ears of corn on display. By midday, a delivery added 54 more ears, and in the afternoon 99 ears were sold to a nearby restaurant. That evening, another delivery brought 42 more ears, and right before closing, 13 ears were given away to a food bank. The remaining ears were then split evenly into 4 crates, with only one crate being kept overnight. The next morning, a wholesale order turned every ear in that crate into 6 ears. How many ears of corn were there after the wholesale order?

In the morning, a bookstore had 189 paperback novels on the clearance table. By midday, 146 novels were sold during a big sale. In the afternoon, a dozen more novels were donated to a local shelter and removed from the table. That evening, the remaining novels doubled when a publisher sent a matching donation. Right before closing, a final donation turned every novel into 4 novels. How many novels were on the clearance table after the final donation?

In the morning, a printing press had 224 flyers ready for a citywide campaign. By midday, a rush order turned every flyer into 4 flyers. In the afternoon, a second rush order turned each of those into 7 flyers. That evening, a final print run turned every flyer into 2 flyers, a run that took '180 minutes, or three hours' to complete. Right after, 3 more flyers were added from a test print. Before the campaign launched, 7703 flyers were distributed across the city. How many flyers were left after the citywide distribution?

Priya had 164 buttons in her craft box, while her classmate Diego had 90 buttons in his. A craft store trade turned every button she had into 6 buttons. She then received 48 more buttons from her grandmother. A school supply drive added 58 more buttons, a collection that took '120 minutes, or two hours' to sort. She then used 60 buttons for a class project. Finally, she donated 606 buttons to the school's art department. How many buttons did Priya have left after the donation?

A beekeeper had 55 frames of honeycomb ready in the spring. He mentioned a dozen new gloves were ordered for the season, though that had nothing to do with the honeycomb count. A strong nectar flow turned every frame into 8 frames. A second hive added 56 more frames. A record harvest then turned every frame into 5 frames. A wholesale buyer then purchased 1898 frames in one large order. How many frames of honeycomb were left after the wholesale order?

Isabella had $183 saved for a school trip, while her friend Noah had $95 saved for the same trip. Isabella earned $65 more from a bake sale, then spent $12 on trip supplies. A matching fund from the school turned every dollar she had into 8 dollars. The trip coordinator mentioned that 20 extra permission slips had also been printed, though that had nothing to do with the money. Isabella then earned $61 more from a car wash fundraiser, and a final grant turned every dollar into 5 dollars. Right before the trip, she received $38 more from her parents. How much money did Isabella have for the trip after receiving money from her parents?

Liam had $232 saved toward a new guitar, while his brother Kai had $150 saved for a drum set. A summer job bonus turned every dollar Liam had into 2 dollars. A holiday bonus then turned every dollar into 3 dollars, a payout that took '60 minutes, or one hour' to process at the bank. He then received $4 more from a birthday card. A final matching program turned every dollar into 3 dollars. How much money did Liam have after the final matching program?

Grace had 56 beads in her bracelet-making kit, while her friend Nora had 40 beads in hers. Grace used 8 beads to finish a small bracelet, then lost 7 beads that rolled under the couch. A craft store gift card added 25 more beads to her kit. Grace's aunt mentioned a dozen extra clasps were also included in a separate order, though that had nothing to do with the bead count. A bead-trading event then turned every bead in her kit into 9 beads, and a second trade turned each of those into 9 beads. A final bonus trade turned every bead into 4 beads. How many beads did Grace have after the final bonus trade?

In the morning, Jonah had 12 marbles in his pocket, while his friend Eli had 30 marbles in his. By midday, a marble machine turned every marble Jonah had into 6 marbles. In the afternoon, a bonus round turned every marble into 2 marbles. That evening, Jonah split his marbles evenly between 2 friends and kept only his own remaining half. Right after, he split what was left evenly between 2 pockets and kept just one pocket's worth. Before heading home, he found 63 more marbles in the schoolyard. How many marbles did Jonah have after finding the marbles in the schoolyard?

In the morning, a movie theater had 234 boxes of candy in the concession stock. By midday, 28 boxes were sold during the matinee. In the afternoon, 98 more boxes were sold during a busy showing. The stock clerk mentioned a dozen new soda cups had also been delivered, though that had nothing to do with the candy count. That evening, the remaining boxes were split evenly into 3 storage bins, and only one bin's stock was tracked overnight. Right before closing, 35 boxes were sold from that bin. How many boxes of candy were left in that bin after closing?

A charity clothing drive had 225 coats collected before winter. The organizer mentioned that 40 scarves were also donated separately, though that had nothing to do with the coat count. A distribution event gave away 173 coats to families in need, and a second event gave away 25 more. A local business then donated 22 more coats, a delivery that took '60 minutes, or one hour' to unload. A school donated 3 more coats, and a church group donated 33 more. How many coats did the charity drive have after the church group's donation?

Owen had 100 sports cards in a binder, while his cousin Leah had 60 cards in hers. Owen traded away 85 cards at a card show. A rare pack he opened turned every remaining card into 4 cards. A second pack turned each of those into 4 cards. He then found 6 more cards under his bed. A final trade turned every card into 4 cards. How many cards did Owen have after the final trade?

A city park had 176 tulip bulbs planted in the spring garden. A volunteer group planted 73 more bulbs the next week, and a garden club added 9 more. A city grant then funded 76 more bulbs for the display. The park ranger mentioned a dozen new garden gloves were also purchased, though that had nothing to do with the bulb count. A bulb-multiplying technique then turned every bulb into 5 bulbs for next season, and the count then tripled again when a botanical garden donated a matching batch. A final community planting event turned every bulb into 7 bulbs. How many tulip bulbs were in the park garden after the final planting event?

In the morning, a fruit stand had 64 crates of peaches ready for sale. By midday, a delivery added 32 more crates, and in the afternoon a bulk harvest turned every crate into 2 crates. That evening, a wholesale deal turned every crate into 7 crates, and right after, 38 more crates arrived from a late delivery. Before closing, 1107 crates were sold to a grocery distributor. After the stand closed for the night, 126 more crates were sent to a food bank. How many crates of peaches were left after the food bank donation?

Maddie had 153 friendship bracelets ready to sell at the school fair, while her partner Grace had 60 bracelets of her own. Maddie sold 87 bracelets in the first hour. The fair organizer mentioned that 40 raffle tickets were also sold, though that had nothing to do with the bracelet count. She then gave away 18 bracelets as prizes for a raffle, and a vendor fee cost her 22 more. A bulk order from a teacher then turned every remaining bracelet into 4 bracelets. She then made 26 more bracelets during a slow period, and a final bulk order from the PTA turned every bracelet into 5 bracelets. How many bracelets did Maddie have after the PTA's bulk order?

A puzzle company had 114 boxes of jigsaw puzzles in a warehouse. A late shipment added 5 more boxes. Then 5 boxes were damaged in a forklift accident and discarded. A big wholesale order then shipped out 112 boxes to a retailer. A new production run turned every remaining box into 6 boxes. The stock then tripled again when a second production line came online. How many boxes of jigsaw puzzles were in the warehouse after the second production line came online?

In the morning, a shoe store had 169 pairs of sneakers in stock. By midday, 79 pairs were sold during a flash sale. In the afternoon, a new shipment turned every remaining pair into 3 pairs. That evening, 85 pairs were sold during a big promotion. Right before closing, 38 more pairs arrived from a late delivery. How many pairs of sneakers were in stock after the late delivery?

In the morning, Dev had 115 seashells in his collection, while his sister Priya had 80 shells in hers. By midday, a shell-multiplying trade turned every shell he had into 8 shells. In the afternoon, he gave away half of them to his beach club, keeping the rest for himself. That evening, he found 3 more shells while walking the shore. Right after, a bonus round turned every shell into 6 shells. Before heading home, a final trade turned every shell into 9 shells, and a second trade turned each of those into 9 more shells. How many shells did Dev have after the second trade?

Nathan had 35 dollars saved for a new skateboard, while his friend Diego had 90 dollars saved for a scooter. A summer job bonus turned every dollar Nathan had into 8 dollars. He then spent 255 dollars on a top-of-the-line skateboard deck. He also paid 15 dollars for new wheels. A birthday gift added 78 more dollars, arriving in an envelope that took '60 minutes, or one hour' to travel by mail from his grandmother. A final matching bonus turned every dollar Nathan had into 2 dollars. How much money did Nathan have after the final matching bonus?
